en: JULIA: \PN?!?!
No!
You can't be!
You must be a shadow clone-- or something!
Please be a shadow clone?
Cuz that would be ~awesome~!
Okay, but, on the realsie-O's,
After you confronted Lin, we all totally thought you disappeared for good!
And... morale was pretty low...
And...
I wasn't captain of the cheer squad for nothing, you know!
Sooooooo I mayyyyyy have told one or two teensy weensy little white lies about what happened to you...
Just to cheer people up, you know?
So if you get some strange reactions...
Don't worry about it!
Great to see you again;
Definitely glad you're not a shadow clone, yep!
JULIA: HIYA!!!!
Oops, sorry for yelling!
I'm in an Extra-Happy-Fun mood now, because BOOMIES!!
Not that I'm not always the extra-cheeriest around,
But explosions make everything better!
Plus, I got to make a new friend!
Y'know, it is kinda unfortunate, though...
That that Corin guy ran off.
I know, I know, he was in big trouble with the police,
And he stood me up,
And sure, maybe he's kiiiind of a notorious thief,
But he was really cute!
Not that I'd ever give him another chance after he stood me up,
But you've gotta admit, it would sure be an exciting relationship!
Aah... It's too bad things with that other guy didn't work out.
Anyhoo, I'm sure you've got things to do, and I've got a fifth cup of coffee to get to.
Enjoy your day, \PN~
JULIA: That circus gig was the best daytrip EVER.
Well, at least since that one date I had a few years ago,
Where we went out to Apophyll and had a water balloon fight and they had to ask us to quiet down because people were trying to meditate or whatever,
But it was pretty amazing!
I TOTALLY wanted to stay longer!
At the circus, I mean.
Buuuut I may have eaten too much cotton candy and felt sick after the Ferris Wheel.
Pro tip: Don't do that.
But it all worked out for you, huh?
That Pokémon was soooo cute.
My Electric-types are still cuter, though. So I don't mind not winning.
But.
That's ONLY this once, understand?
Don't get used to that kind of attitude.
I'm still the best, peppiest battler, and the peppiest, best battler!
So don't forget it!
JULIA: Okay, so, here's the itinerary for Rini and me:
I'm thinking, we see if we can fly on fireworks next week.
By the month after, we'll probaly have recovered from any burns we sustained, so we can try going to the rodeo--
Get this--
AS the bulls.
I know you might think that's silly but I know a guy and he says he can make a Tauros fursuit that is ABSOLUTELY indistinguishable.
After that, we're thinking of either skiing down Ametrine,
Snowboarding down it,
Or trying to do both at the same time.
Oh, and a bit after that, I got concert tickets!
Unrelated, I happened to meet an event planner who told me where a certain orchestra stores their instruments in between performances.
So I'm considering two different arrangements right now-- tell me what you think!
Okay, option one:
Bubblefoam in EVERYTHING.
The tubas especially will love it,
But I think people are underselling the trombones.
Option two:
Bubbles in the tubas and trombones only, confetti in the other brasses and woodwinds, and Verdignite in one specific drum.
Eeeh?
Eeeeeeh?
She's gonna love it.
It's nice to have someone who you know will be there for you in the future instead of having to cling to the past!
That's why communication is important!
Also bubbles!
JULIA: A one, two, three, four~
Give me TNT if you want some more~
JULIA: THIS IS MY SONG!!!
JULIA: C'mon, \PN, show me how you work it!
JULIA: This place always has the best music!
JULIA: Let's blow this place up!
FLORINIA: Greetings again, \PN.
I am... relieved to see you well.
This speaker is grateful to see you return unharmed.
There are two reasons therefore:
First, it is only natural to be concerned about another's well-being after an untimely disappearance...
However...
While the obvious level degree of human sympathy naturally still takes precedence and priority,
An additional selfish aspect exists.
It's... Julia.
She has repeatedly attempted to correlate your disappearance to a variety of statistically impossible causes.
It is... what some would probably call obnoxious.
Maddening, perhaps.
And because I alone have continued to doubt the validity of her claims, she has made it a personal undertaking to repeat them as much as possible,
And in increasing magnitudes of improbability...
Julia has repeatedly attempted to correlate your disappearance to a variety of statistically impossible causes.
When this speaker did not believe her initial suggestion, she tried again.
And when the second trial produced additional failure, she continued.
The only worthwhile comment that can be said of any of it is that persistence is rivaled only by the sheer magnitude of her ridiculousness.
Therefore, additional gratitude for your return is warranted.
Thank you for inadvertently rescuing us.
FLORINIA: This is all very difficult to process fully.
Emotions are ultimately mere electrical stimulation on a biological hardware.
Even then, what part of that electricity-- what neurotransmitter is responsible for,
The peace that the system feels upon accepting itself?
What evolutionary mechanism had already adapted to protect even the very concept of mechanisms?
And even naming the specific chemicals and voltages involved, the routes they trace--
How should such things influence my perception as a conscious being?
Why is it my eyes that I, as a conscious being, see through?
What makes my emotions so special that they need to be felt more than anyone else's?
All of the questions...
...Don't have answers, do they?
No amount of science or study is equal to the task of solving them.
No, it's better to simply accept the way things are, and enjoy the lightness of it all.
There can be peace even under siege.
FLORINIA: I am grateful to not have closed the proverbial book on my former friends entirely.
It is perhaps lamentable how regularly they require one to go in and avail themselves of their own drama, but...
I suppose that is what some refer to as being the...
..."Mom friend"...
...I do not know how I feel about that phrase.
Julia appears to be planning something sinister.
...Against my better judgment, I am rather looking forward to finding out what it may be.
FLORINIA: There's too much to identify.
A solution of hope and fear and relief and anxiety,
But independent of all of those feelings together, I can say with confidence that I'm glad he's back.
No analysis was necessary to settle on that conclusion.
FLORINIA: ...\PN?
Something has happened?
Fern has--
...Understood.
FLORINIA: I am glad to see that you are unharmed.
Actually, I had wanted to ask you about something.
Since the emergence of this 'New World', in addition to various Legendaries,
Creatures known as 'Ultra Beasts' have been appearing as well.
I've been... curious, I suppose,
About the differences between them, and would much appreciate the chance to inspect any further instances of them you might encounter.
FLORINIA: This speaker recognizes the dangers you have faced, and is glad that you have emerged unharmed.
A query:
Since the emergence of the phenomenon known as the 'New World', in addition to the presence of an unusual number of Legendary Pokémon,
Reports of the creatures known as 'Ultra Beasts' have also been received.
While this speaker has encountered one so far, further study of multiple samples is merited to ascertain validity of prior observations.
Have you encountered any such creatures?
Interesting.
May I see?
A moment, while this speaker examines the relevant data...
FLORINIA: Interesting.
Your assistance is greatly appreciated.
FLORINIA: The pertinent data has been downloaded from your Pokédex.
FLORINIA: Please return if you find an Ultra Beast.
A shame.
If you encounter any, I would appreciate if you would tell me.
I find the creatures quite interesting.
If the subject encounters any such beings at any time in the future, this speaker would be interested in knowing.
FLORINIA: Thank you for your help.
I have been fascinated by these creatures for some time now.
Thank you.
I've acquired a few of these specialized Poke Balls since all of this began.
To show my gratitude, I would like you to have some.
FLORINIA: Your assistance is appreciated.
The opportunity to study this data will prove invaluable.
In return, please accept this.
A small number had been collected to aid in study, and it would perhaps aid you in your endeavors as well.
FLORINIA: So Fern has decided to loiter around this place now too...
...Perhaps it is for the best that he is no longer hiding his face.
There is...
...A surplus of confounding emotional information--
Er, that is to say...
I'm... not sure what to feel right now.
FLORINIA: There will always be uncertainties and confounding variables...
To gather all of one's anxieties and face them head- first...
Perhaps that's what luck is for.
FLORINIA: I appreciate you taking the moment to check on me.
FLORINIA: This place is still a little...
Overstimulating.
Still, I would rather be here with everyone than not.
FLORINIA: Good day.
What do you require?
SHELLY: \PN, is it really you?
You're back, safe and sound, truly?
Huh...
Don't get me wrong-- I'm relieved you're back...
But to be honest, I'm also a little disappointed.
I heard that you'd fallen into a Darkrai's nightmare and it wouldn't let you wake up!
And-- And I wanted, you know, since you had always been going around saving everyone...
Um, I was thinking that, this time, maybe it would be nice if I could be your hero instead.
I've been going on a lot of Legendary hunts, hoping I'd eventually run into that Darkrai--
...But if you're back, I guess it's already dealt with.
And that's what's most important-- that you're here.
I'm so glad you made it! Welcome back!
SHELLY: D-don't tell me...
I heard about what happened...
\PN... You were attacked by a Darkrai again?
And-- and I still wasn't here to help!
I suppose it's probably easier after you've done it once...
B-but still! That's twice I've missed my chance!
And of course, twice you've been taken!
I'm not sure why Darkrai keep coming after you, but they need to stop!
Maybe-- maybe it was the same one? And now that you've caught it, it will leave you alone!
I hope so, anyway...
B-but don't worry, \PN!
I know I missed the first two times, but I promise,
Someday I'm going to be a hero.
I've gotten so much stronger, and so much braver...
I'm going to keep helping people!
SHELLY: But, um--
Please do be careful.
A-and maybe... stay away from Darkrai out there.
Just in case it wasn't only the one, and more are angry with you for some reason.
Even if you can break out, nightmares aren't very nice.
SHELLY: \PN?
I was wondering-- did you really go and time travel?
Heather wouldn't stop talking about it after she'd gone to ask Simon about what happened...
Um, and I just had to ask for myself!
I'd heard that you met Heather and her mom, and I was, um... wondering if-- if I was there, too?
I-I mean, you don't have to tell me or anything!
SHELLY: O-oh! You really met my future self?
What was the future like?
What was I like?
Did you have a nice time?
SHELLY: No, no, don't tell me!
I know the future of Reborn has to have been so bright thanks to you and everything you've done, after all!
With all the Anomalies that are popping up--
I know there'll be more that I can help out with in the future!
I know that you were able to see the future yourself--
But I want to find what's in my future on my own-- whatever it'll turn out to be!
SHELLY: I'm glad everything went okay out at Rhodochrine.
I-- I went over everything in the Underroot, just to be extra sure.
Everything seems to be back in order now!
I'm sure that's thanks to everything you all did up top!
I'm so happy for Noel...
I just wish I'd been able to do more to help.
D-don't worry, though!
I know there'll be more to do in the future!
And I'll be the first one in line to help out!
SHELLY: Oh hi, \PN!
Heather and I were just talking about helping with some more of those Anomalies in a bit.
I wonder what will turn up next!
SHELLY: I wonder how that Kricketot is doing...
SHELLY: Don't worry about me.
I know what I have to do now.
I'll keep getting stronger, in battle and as a person.
I owe it to myself.
SHELLY: I love helping out here, but it's not the easiest place to read...
SHELLY: Thanks for being my friend!
I'm so grateful to all of you.
SHADE: Fortune favors the forsaken, but few find the forsaken be such forever.
SHADE: ...
HARDY: Oi, \PN, is that really you?
Or... Uh, haha, man, I don't know-- I don't know how to talk to you now.
AYA: Forgive him, he left his brain at home.
Just talk to \PN like you always have.
They obviously still understand human language, even if they're a Pokémon.
HARDY: Like, I don't wanna be rude, mate--
Is it weird to call a Pokémon "mate"?
Man, I've just got so many questions...
AYA: Then just ask them, since \PN is here again for some reason.
HARDY: All right, all right...
So, it's true that you've just been a Zoroark in disguise this whole time?
AYA: Obviously they wouldn't admit that.
HARDY: Wow, mate, I--
Er, stow it, I'm just gonna keep saying that same as I always have.
So, do you like, have a Trainer, or nah?
HARDY: I suppose a Pokémon as strong as you's gotta have one, huh.
HARDY: Makes sense...
After all, Julia said that since your work to save humankind was done, you went back to the wild.
But if that's true, then why are you here?
AYA: Be honest, did you miss us?
AYA: Don't lie.
HARDY: C'mon, if \PN says they missed us, then they missed us.
You gotta learn to accept compliments at face value or you'll never feel better about yourself.
'S rude to just call people-- er... Pokémon-- liars, especially if they really are tellin' the truth.
AYA: Ugh, I know, shut up.
Don't actually shut up.
I just-- fine.
I missed you too, \PN.
Even if you did trick us all.
HARDY: Don't you worry about that, mate.
HARDY: Cold, but no sweat-- I know it's gotta be a bit rough tryna get along with a bunch of humans.
For what it's worth, you had us all completely fooled.
Don't worry about that, though!
We're happy to have you around as long as you still wanna be.
AYA: That whole rehearsal was way too much for one afternoon.
But I'm glad.
Tez got put in his stupid place,
And I'm pretty sure if I can deal with the entire Genesect Legion, I can deal with a perpetually-buzzed ball of cholesterol and rage.
Still no plans on being home more than necessary, but if I have to be...
I'll be fine.
AYA: Hey, by the way, thanks for saving my stupid baby brother.
Don't tell him I said that.
...No, you can tell him.
Ugh, the point is,
I'm relieved, okay?
AYA: I'm glad you're okay.
I'm... really sorry about what happened on that train.
When Hardy and I first ran into those orbs, I thought they were kind of pretty.
But even then-- they were more hassle than anything.
The Red Orb was so heavy, and it kept randomly getting heavier and lighter--
And at one point it got hot?
It burned Hardy's pocket.
And the Blue Orb...
We had to keep it between us.
You've seen firsthand what that one does.
I’m just glad nobody got really hurt.
It would've been so awful...
Although I won't lie to you--
I'm glad I wasn't there.
I'm glad I didn't have to be the one to deal with Terra again.
My head hurt for ages after the first time we met,
And her mallet didn't help either.
Anyway, thanks for dealing with that.
Hopefully there's no more trouble with those things.
HARDY: Yo, Aya, wanna dance?
AYA: ...Not really.
I don't really dance that much.
HARDY: Aite, no problem.
Just sittin' here's kinda nice, too.
AYA: Yeah, it is.
AYA: Thanks for asking, though.
AYA: I've heard a few remixes of this beat.
I can get behind this one though.
AYA: People-watching isn't so bad.
Especially if you're not afraid to be seen back, I guess.
AYA: Thanks for still being around.
AYA: I like these places in theory more than I like actually being here.
But maybe that's just for lack of familiarity.
SERRA: Now here's a sight for sore eyes.
I just have one question for you, \PN.
Was there really a movie?
Or was that just a line?
SERRA: Heh. I figured.
A while after you disappeared, Julia 'let slip' that you'd been scouted by Pokéstar Studios.
Wasn't sure what to think.
But really, I should've known.
Anyway.
We're both working on these Anomalies, so I'm sure we'll run into each other.
SERRA: That... sure was something, huh?
I'm... still not sure how to feel about it.
I've been working on embracing positivity more for a while now,
And... that was kind of inspiring, back there, honestly.
To let the light flow through me.
Literally.
But at the same time, I know how ridiculous that sounds.
It makes me feel like some kind of hippie, putting it that way.
But it's kind of hard to phrase it any other way.
I don't know.
It's a work in progress.
But I feel like I'm getting there.
It's getting easier to see the good in things, anyway.
It's a nice feeling.
Even with how much of a debacle that whole thing with Necrozma was,
I'm very glad I was there.
...Just, do me a favor?
Don't let Radomus know I said all that.
I've got a feeling that man could be pretty damn smug when he's right about something, and I don't feel like finding out just how smug.
SERRA: That trip from Aegir Cave is NOT a short one.
Made for a nice workout, but I'm glad these seats are soft.
...Still,
That was a good time, out there.
Bennett's grown so much.
He's made some bad choices, but he seems to be doing well now.
And that was the first I've gotten to just spend time with him in...
Well, a long time. Long before he left home.
Don't get me wrong.
I still hate that old priest, or whatever he's calling himself,
But... look at Bennett.
Sometimes I wonder if that Elias did more for him than I ever did.
I guess there's no use thinking too hard about it.
Just got to work on being grateful for what I've got now.
That's not something that comes easily to me,
But after that camping trip?
I am grateful.
SERRA: You're quite the local celebrity, you know that?
No, not the Champion thing.
Since you went up to the circus, trounced the competition as usual, and caught that Meloetta.
I have to say.
I'm not happy about all these Anomalies all over the place, but...
To draw a crowd that size?
That Pokémon has some stage presence.
It's kind of wild that she got so many people wanting her autograph after only one show.
I'm almost jealous in a way.
Ha...
Well, I hope she enjoys the attention.
From what I've heard, she's got talent enough to take her far.
SERRA: This is a nice change of pace, actually.
I haven't heard music like this in years.
SERRA: There's a part of me that wants to join the dance again...
...And then there's a part of me that's just going to feel old if I continue that sentence.
SERRA: Not that I mind, but don't you have better things to do than dawdle about with me?
SERRA: Thanks for looking out for everyone.
For a kid, you've got quite a sense of responsibility on you.
SERRA: This place reminds me of the runways.
The lights especially.
God, I miss them.
NOEL: Hi, \PN.
Thanks.
For waking us up back there, I mean.
Seems like you keep doing that.
Of all places to get stuck...
Julia told me you "ascended to another plane of existence."
She said the Unown make everything there...
I wasn't sure if I should believe it, honestly.
I guess she was just making things up.
Either way, it's good to see you.
NOEL: Thanks for finding Radomus.
I didn't like the terms we left on before.
I can do better now.
NOEL: I was thinking about earlier.
I'm really glad I was invited to that picnic.
I'm not sure I would've met Xerneas otherwise.
I know Anna interrupted,
I know Lin interrupted,
But I'm glad Xerneas and I were able to understand each other.
NOEL: Thanks for finishing the job before.
Things will be better now.
After all, now I'm the only kid running around with completely unrestrained magical powers.
That was a joke.
Don't worry, I won't do anything unnecessary.
Unless...
NOEL: That was also a joke.
But I think it's good to leave just a little bit of magic in the world.
Maybe I can only say that because I'm still a kid,
But if everything could really be explained by things like logic and numbers,
Wouldn't adults get bored of that way too fast?
They're the ones that need the magic the most.
NOEL: This place is loud.
Kind of like the Railnet.
I don't like the noise, but it's not awful.
At least with the Anomalies, there are things I can do.
NOEL: If nothing is real, then the world is a blank canvas.
What picture would you like to be painted?
NOEL: I thought everyone just looked at me like my own sister's keeper.
I know I was wrong to think that.
They wanted to look at me that way because they wanted a keeper too.
NOEL: Anna is her own person, and she doesn't need me to watch her.
I'm my own person too.
So I'm glad that we can still look out for each other.
NOEL: It's too bad.
They can't always do what they want,
Because no one can see all they've done.
Not even all the people they've helped.
RADOMUS: Good day, \PN.
As always, it is a pleasure to see you again,
Even if our last meeting was under... less than fortuitous circumstances.
I do hope you will not hold it too much against me,
Though I of course would not, and could not, blame you if you did.
RADOMUS: I meant what I said, however.
I will do everything within my power to find a way to make things right.
For all of them.
And in the meantime...
It will be good to reconnect with Noel,
And of course, the friends I had left behind in this world.
I do hope you will stop by again.
RADOMUS: You have my thanks, once again, for helping Noel.
I cannot pretend not to be... frustrated... at how little I was able to help,
But the feeling is quite fleeting.
I am the first one to admit how badly I have failed, when it comes to my son,
But... I could not be more proud of him.
I do not expect him to believe me, not now, but I hope, in time, I will be able to prove it to him.
RADOMUS: I must say, this is not my regular choice of music.
...Not entirely unknown, however.
I believe I have heard this exact song once before, on Gardevoir's show.
It's a bit remarkable, actually.
Nonetheless, I believe I shall ask if Mr. Arclight takes requests.
A brief change would not be at all unwelcome.
RADOMUS: \PN...
Truly, I cannot thank you enough.
You've done what I could never do--
Both in regards to Team Meteor, and in bringing my children to safety.
You can't know what it means to have this second chance--
No, I suspect it's more of a third or fourth chance now.
In any case, I am more than delighted that it is here.
So...
From the bottom of my heart-- thank you.
RADOMUS: I wonder if Obsidia Department Store has received any new stock recently.
The chance for a new hat would be welcome.
RADOMUS: You must stop by for a game sometime.
RADOMUS: I'm glad your head has remained level through all of this.
RADOMUS: This has been a learning experience for all of us.
It's been fascinating to see how everyone has grown.
RADOMUS: It truly is a delight to see Luna thriving so.
LUNA: How do you do, \PN?
It seems some fantastical rumors have been swirling around in our respective absences.
When I first returned here ahead of you, Julia told me you had willingly been imprisoned on the moon.
Something about sealing Lin in there so that humanity's negative energy could never reach her to give her power.
"That's nonsense," I told her,
"I was just at the moon but a few days prior--
Not a soul there."
Of course, I'm not one to doubt the possibilities.
Do you plan on going to the moon any time soon yourself?
I hear the dark side is lovely this time of year.
If you do visit, I should very much like to go with you.
In the meantime, I believe we can settle for a few more New World expeditions.
LUNA: You have my sincerest thanks for having found my father as such.
I am ever-heartened to have both of my parents back home safely in time for supper.
Of course, it's not as if I was worried.
There is no embarrassment or bluster here;
Only faith.
Neither time nor distance is a threat to ties that bind.
And yet, it is nice to have them close at hand.
LUNA: \PN... Are you well?
I can't say I'm entirely aware of the details, but I know there was a Darkrai recently...
I was at least vaguely aware that there was some manner of deception and foul play afoot...
And yet, powerless to stop it.
It was something like looking inwards at a jail cell.
And the jailer...
Well, if it weren't for the way he treated you, I would almost daresay he was quite personally intriguing.
But the entire manner is unforgivable, and you may be very sure I was far from thrilled when he borrowed my likeness to deceive you.
I am sorry to have been any part of that in your memory, even if not by my own will.
You can be sure you are quite all here in reality now.
Please be well.
LUNA: I do... hope that you will keep at least somewhat quiet about all that you may have seen at the sanctum.
There are many things I find comfort in forgetting.
It is a bitter pill to be forced to swallow, to be reminded of such matters from outside oneself.
LUNA: You have my true and dearest thanks, \PN.
I see that Ace is safe and with us once more, and I am ever-grateful for this fact.
They have... provided a network of support and care that is a comfort to have close by once more,
And I only wish I could have expressed the same earlier.
We are always bereft of the time that we seek to share with others,
...And then we are only privy to realize that after the time is simply too far gone.
I find myself deeply regretful and disappointed that I could not do more to aid with their rescue.
I owe them thanks that cannot be repaid enough for what transpired so long ago at the sanctum.
...But perhaps it is nothing that cannot be made up from now on, after all.
Lost time can always be repaid.
LUNA: I have made it plainly clear I would rather forget my biological father entirely.
And what a distasteful word-- "biological"--
I'm sure there are innocuous uses of it yet, but I struggle to associate it with science over personal irritation.
It is always used in cases of trying to assert truths of some matter or another which one cannot truly know.
Nevertheless, I come to doubt the ethics of my ignorance.
Perhaps for the sake of another person, I can demonstrate undeserved tolerance.
But he will want more from me than I wish to offer him.
Just how far should one go for something like that...
